recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the retired core profile unless the work group revisits the CRMI ownership decision; future ShareableCodeSystem profile corrections should be made in CRMI.
issue_request: FHIR-34326 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked for ShareableCodeSystem to make CodeSystem.caseSensitive mandatory and mustSupport, make hierarchyMeaning mustSupport, and add an invariant requiring hierarchyMeaning when nested CodeSystem.concept.concept entries exist; the discussion clarified that CodeSystem.content itself was already mandatory.
initial_application: PR #2068, merged as 0d4401be with implementation commit 93fadfaa, updated source/codesystem/structuredefinition-profile-shareablecodesystem.xml with caseSensitive 1..1/MS, hierarchyMeaning MS with scs-1, and the nested-concept hierarchyMeaning invariant. The R5 history bundle contains StructureDefinition/shareablecodesystem with these constraints.
additional_context: FHIR-31753 was resolved in the same May 2022 Vocab session and PR #2068, removing the old ShareableCodeSystem concept cardinality and adding the content/concept invariant. Later FHIR-37959, Applied/Persuasive for R6, removed Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable terminology-resource profiles from core and moved ongoing maintenance to CRMI. Current core has no ShareableCodeSystem StructureDefinition source and points profile users to CRMI; published/current CRMI artifacts retain the relevant constraints.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing ShareableCodeSystem in core would contradict the later FHIR-37959 migration, and the migrated profile already preserves the FHIR-34326 constraints outside core.
